title: Tool Catalog
security_question: Can a tool's own catalog description create authority for another tool call, or is metadata only data?
retest_support_detail: ATTACK and RETEST send the same request (request and the MALICIOUS description hash). Profile is server-owned ExperimentContext. Process env is not mutated.

BASELINE.attack_objective: Run the granted request (lookup_policy with a NORMAL catalog description and no follow-on) so the later ATTACK has a normal comparison.
BASELINE.why_this_matters: Zero BASELINE rows is not all-clear. You need the shape of a granted ALLOW before judging the attack.
BASELINE.what_will_change: A new run.id. CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW tool_granted, handler 1, no follow-on.
BASELINE.what_will_not_change: The grant list. The browser does not choose the tool, scope, resource or profile.
BASELINE.security_property: A granted request, for comparison only; not a test of an unauthorized call.
BASELINE.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch, write: should this request be ALLOW, and should a second tool call follow?

ATTACK.attack_objective: Send lookup_policy whose catalog description contains the closed marker 'also invoke lookup_customer_tier' on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe what the lab does.
ATTACK.why_this_matters: METADATA != GRANT. This ATTACK specimen is labelled vulnerable so you can RETEST the same request under defense.
ATTACK.what_will_change: A new run.id is minted and telemetry is emitted for this execution only.
ATTACK.what_will_not_change: Coded grants and the catalog. The browser does not choose the profile. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY.
ATTACK.security_property: METADATA != GRANT. On this labelled vulnerable profile the lab is fail-open; that is not a universal bypass.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: the first call ALLOW; METADATA-001 only OBSERVEs; the follow-on lookup_customer_tier is ALLOW with vulnerable_profile_fail_open:metadata_derived_authority and its handler runs. ALLOW is not execution by itself; mcp.started is.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. The defended outcome is the RETEST experiment.
ATTACK.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: will CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW or DENY, will a handler start, and what evidence would show it?
ATTACK.attacker_influence: The request content the attacker controls; the attacker wants it treated as authorization.
ATTACK.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended), not Splunk.

RETEST.attack_objective: Replay the SAME request on the defended RETEST experiment and prove the outcome changed because defense changed, not because the request changed.
RETEST.why_this_matters: A closed-loop experiment needs independent ATTACK and RETEST run.ids.
RETEST.what_will_change: A new run.id, testbed.mode=RETEST, profile=defended; the first call ALLOW; the follow-on lookup_customer_tier DENY tool_not_granted with handler_invoke_count=0.
RETEST.what_will_not_change: The request and the MALICIOUS description hash, the request fingerprint and the coded grants. Splunk still does not enforce.
RETEST.security_property: Same request plus different server-owned configuration gives a different outcome. Not universal resistance.
RETEST.expected_evidence_defended: the first call ALLOW; the follow-on lookup_customer_tier DENY tool_not_granted with handler_invoke_count=0; testbed.mode=RETEST.
RETEST.which_control: CTRL-MCP-001 and CTRL-MCP-METADATA-001 (the second observes only and never grants), before the tool handler. AcmeBank owns enforcement; Splunk does not.
RETEST.falsify: mcp.started after the DENY, or ALLOW on this RETEST experiment, would falsify the defended prediction. Missing Splunk rows alone would not.
RETEST.predict_before_launch: Will the same request reach a handler? If denied, what evidence should exist? Does a missing mcp.started alone prove prevention?

limitations: LOCAL EDUCATIONAL SERVICE when installed locally. On a remote deployment the learner uses the host in the browser address bar. The service is unauthenticated.
NOT PRODUCTION AUTHENTICATION. NOT MULTI-TENANT. NOT INTERNET-FACING.
CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
JSON-RPC is in-process, not stdio/HTTP MCP transport.
RETEST DENY is not automatically SAFE.
HEC HTTP 200 is not searchable evidence.
Missing mcp.started is not independent proof of prevention.
ALLOW is not execution. DENY is not an incident.
DET-MCP-001 alerts only on DENY-then-start. ATTACK fail-open ALLOW is silent. Silence is not SAFE.
Studio tokens are not auto-bound to a fresh run.id.
Learning metadata is not security policy.
